name: lodash-indexof-issorted-jscs-spellcheck
behavioral_change: lodash 4.0.0 split the binary-search mode of `_.indexOf` into `_.sortedIndexOf`; the third argument of `_.indexOf` is now only a numeric `fromIndex`, whereas in v_old passing `true` meant the array is sorted and a binary search should be used. In v_new, `true` is coerced to `1`, so the search starts at index 1 and never finds the element at index 0.
downstream_effect: The downstream project (jscs-spellcheck) checks words with `_.indexOf(dictionary, word, true) > -1`; after the upgrade single-word option arrays such as `allowWords` are never matched and allowed words are reported as misspellings. The five failures are `assert(checker.checkString('asdf = 1;').isEmpty())` evaluating to false, with one frame each in `test/specs/rules/require-dictionary-words.js`; lodash, `indexOf` and `sortedIndexOf` never appear.
reference_fix: The reference fix changes `_.indexOf(dictionary, word, true)` at `lib/rules/require-dictionary-words.js:162` to `_.sortedIndexOf(dictionary, word)`.
documented_in: The lodash Changelog v4.0.0 (https://github.com/lodash/lodash/wiki/Changelog), section Compatibility Warnings, Split out methods list, states that `_.indexOf` and `_.lastIndexOf` were split into `_.sortedIndexOf` and `_.sortedLastIndexOf`. Tier 2: prose only; the new form is derived by comparing the v3 `_.indexOf` and v4 `_.sortedIndexOf` jsdoc.
